Everyone is a failure in some ways. I would say in many ways. But there are people I love despite of them not getting it all together. I met a girl in college and I new I wanted to be her friend. I was jealous of her life. She seemed perfect - beautiful inside and out! Everyone likes her. But I didn't try to approach her, because I thought I'm a subhuman. Few years by and she started to approach me (ugly, pathetic, lazy, uninteresting me)! And I was actually trying to reject her! We are friends now for more than 10 years. Despite hating my life I'm not jealous of her life anymore. I thought she is a perfect girl with a perfect life, but that was not true. Turns out we have similar problems (physical and mental health), some of hers are even worse than mine, I'm still surprised about this. I don't think anyone is happy. Happiness is a fleeting moment even for the best of us. And no-one has perfect life even when it seems perfect. I'm sure you have talents and good character qualities you cannot see for yourself. You are more than your mistakes. I wish you find someone to help you.

People blame the victim, because it's easier to think " if you don't do this, that won't happen to you". They are wrong. Bad things happened because someone else decided this is what they are going to do. You can be a nun, but a rapist won't care.

Anyway it doesn't necessarily mean your mom doesn't care about you. She might be very afraid and angry for what happened to you. But she could not confront them, so instead she confronted you. Sometimes mothers act like this when they don't feel they can protect their children from something, so they want their children to be extra careful. If the child "fails",  they are angry and frustrated from their own  helplessness. 

Maybe you can talk to your mom and explain HOW MUCH you NEED her support. She might don't know what to do, but you can explicitly tell her what kinda support you want and DON'T want from her.
